catalog_quote: Die Betonung wird mit Akut /´/, unbetonte Endungen in Tabellen ggf. mit Gravis /`/, Nasalierungen mit hochgestelltem /ⁿ/ ... gekennzeichnet. Da im Zaz. Feminina auf -ε ~ -ɨ und -i im Auslaut unbetont sind, werden sie meistens als solche nicht angegeben, stattdessen wird die vorletzte Silbe betont gekennzeichnet, z.B. kέrgε „Henne“, kárdi „Messer“. Feminina auf -a oder in Mundarten mit ε-Apokope werden gekennzeichnet. Bei Maskulina auf betontem -ε ~ ɨ, i oder u erübrigt sich ebenfalls die Angabe des Genus. (pp. 19-20) ... Ebenfalls taucht beim Akzentwechsel von der letzen auf die erste Silbe im Vokativ eine Labialisierung auf: Qεrεmán „Kahraman (Männername ‚Held’)“ Rct. Sg.: Qέrεmuⁿ! Vok. Sg. (p. 61) ... Eine Akzentverschiebung auf die vorige Silbe aufgrund der Synkope des schwachen ɨ, besonders beim Diminutivs -ɨ, wie auch in West-Dersim (Ov., Hz.), ist ziemlich gängig, wie etwa in: xálε „Tante (mütterlicherseits)“, Plm. xalɨ́ε; láwε „Lied“, Plm. lawɨ́ε. (p. 114) ... Wie in der bisherigen Dialektologie üblich, wird auf die Lexik und Syntax weniger, auf die prosodischen Merkmale (auch aufgrund des Forschungsstands) gar nicht eingegangen, obwohl sich Mundarten oft gerade gerne in der Satzmelodie und der Betonung unterscheiden. (p. 12)

new_statements.translation: Stress is marked with an acute, unstressed endings in tables where necessary with a grave [...]. Since in Zazaki feminines ending in -ε ~ -ɨ and -i are unstressed word-finally, they are mostly not marked as such; instead the penultimate syllable is marked as stressed, e.g. kέrgε 'hen', kárdi 'knife'. [...] With masculines in stressed -ε ~ ɨ, i or u the indication of gender is likewise unnecessary. (p. 19) — Likewise, with the accent shift from the last to the first syllable in the vocative, a labialisation appears: Qεrεmán 'Kahraman (man's name, Hero)' rectus sg. : Qέrεmu! vocative sg. (p. 61)
new_statements.citation: Keskin, Mesut. 2008. Zur dialektalen Gliederung des Zazaki. Magisterarbeit, Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main. 204 pp. (open:https://www.zazaki.de/files/Mesut-Keskin-Zur-dialektalen-Gliederung-des-Zazaki.pdf)
new_statements.locator: §4 Transkription, p. 19 (p. 19); vocative remark p. 61 (p. 61); syncope remark p. 114 (p. 114)
new_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (symlink to, 204 pp., text) and extracted pp. 12, 19, 20, 61, 114 with extracted text. The quoted passages are there: p. 19 (§4 Transkription) reads verbatim "Die Betonung wird mit Akut /´/, unbetonte Endungen in Tabellen ggf. mit Gravis /`/.. gekennzeichnet. Da im Zaz. Feminina auf -ε ~ -ɨ und -i im Auslaut unbetont sind, werden sie meistens als solche nicht angegeben, stattdessen wird die vorletzte Silbe betont gekennzeichnet, z.B. kέrgε „Henne", kárdi „Messer"." Minor differences: the bridged sentence "Bei Maskulina auf betontem -ε ~ ɨ, i oder u erübrigt sich ebenfalls die Angabe des Genus." is at the top of p. 20, not p. 19; the vocative example on p. 61 is printed Qέrεmu with a…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is on the final syllable by default (masculine stems ending in -e/-ɨ/-i/-u carry final stress and the author marks stress only where it deviates); the feminine endings -e/-ɨ/-i are inherently unstressed, so such feminines are stressed on the penult (kέrge, kárdi). The vocative moves the accent from the last to the first syllable; syncope of a weak ɨ shifts the accent one syllable leftwards (xálε vs Pülümür xalɨ́ε).
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed feminine endings -e/-ɨ/-i (penult stress); vocative with initial stress; accent retraction after syncope of weak ɨ; unstressed enclitics/postpositions (-dɨ, -i 'also') and unstressed inflectional endings noted in passing.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation/lexical forms in a dialectological transcription convention; the author states (p. 12) that prosody is deliberately not treated because of the state of research, so the final-stress default is implied by the marking convention rather than stated as a phonological rule. The remarks apply to Zazaki generally with Northern Zazaki (Dersim/Varto/Pülümür/Ovacık/Hozat) examples.
new_statements.identity_note: Keskin 2008 describes all Zazaki dialects with its main focus on Northern Zazaki (Dersim, Erzincan, Varto, Hınıs, Pülümür, Ovacık, Hozat) = kirm1248; the transcription statement is phrased for Zazaki in general, the vocative example is from the Northern (Dersim/Erzincan) area. The other full grammars are on the Southern dialect: Todd 1985 (Çermik/Siverek) and Paul 1998 Part I (Çermik-Siverek) = Dimli/Southern Zazaki, Glottolog diml1238; Paul 1998's 'Alevi-Dialekte' section is the Northern part. Selcan 1998 is Dersim (kirm1248) throughout.

tone_statements.citation: Kırkan, Ahmet. 2019. Zazacanın fonetik açıdan incelenmesi; Kuzey, güney ve merkez Zazacasının karşılaştırılması [A phonetic study of Zazaki; comparison of Northern, Southern and Central Zazaki]. Doktora tezi (PhD thesis), Dicle Üniversitesi, Sosyal Bilimler Enstitüsü, Kürt Dili ve Kültürü Anabilim Dalı, Diyarbakır (advisor Hayreddin Kızıl). 591 pp. YÖK tez no. 554401. (in Turkish)
tone_statements.quote: Bazı dillerde ton çok önemlidir. Örnek olarak yalınlayan diller olarak bilinen Çince, Tayland Dili, Tibet Dili, Vietnam Dili gibi tek heceli diller, ton dilleri olarak bilinirler. … Örnek olarak, “Ti senîn mi kenê xo vîr ra.” cümlesini kızgınlık, şaşırma, sitem, soru gibi anlamları yüklemek istediğimizde, cümleyi farklı şekillerde tonlarız. … Tonlama, cümlenin tamamını etkilediği gibi, çoğu kez, kendinden sonra gelen cümlelerin duygu rengine de tesir eder. … Sadece ünlemler değil, cümledeki her sözcük, tonlamayla farklı anlam ilişkileri içerisine girer.
tone_statements.translation: In some languages tone is very important. For example, monosyllabic languages known as isolating languages, such as Chinese, Thai, Tibetan and Vietnamese, are known as tone languages. … For example, when we want to load the sentence 'Ti senîn mi kenê xo vîr ra.' with meanings such as anger, surprise, reproach or question, we intone the sentence in different ways. … Intonation affects the whole sentence and often also the emotional colour of the sentences that follow it. … Not only interjections but every word in the sentence enters into different meaning relations through intonation.

tone.quote: Asta suprasegmentale ziwanî ra ziwanî vurîyêna û na aste de hîna zêde eleman û taybetmendîyî estê. Ziwanî derb, ton, melodî, rîtîm, lezîye, ding, tini û hece sey elemanê na aste yenê qebul kerdene ... Na xebate de yewineyê asta suprasegmentalî ra derb (teql, vurgu) ameyo îzah kerdene. ... Derb hîrê şeklan a yeno meydan. Nînan ra yew; heceyêke, heceyanê bînan ra hîna pêt û eşkera yena vatene. Derb zafane no tewirî ya yeno meydan. Rayîra bîne de derb bi tonê vengî ya yeno meydan.
tone.locator: p. 451, section on the suprasegmental level; last three sentences p. 453, section 'Derb (teql, vurgu)'
tone.translation: The suprasegmental level varies from language to language and at this level there are more elements and features. In language, stress, tone, melody, rhythm, tempo, juncture, timbre and syllable are accepted as elements of this level ... In this study, of the units of the suprasegmental level, stress (teql, vurgu) has been explained. ... Stress arises in three ways. One of them: a syllable is pronounced more strongly and clearly than the other syllables. Stress mostly arises in this way. In another way stress arises through the tone of the voice.

Lexical tone or pitch accent is nowhere mentioned; the suprasegmental treatment is stress-only.

tone.quote: Guvaş di axaftinê de çê dibe û gelek jî girîng e. Guvaş hem li ser kiteyê hem jî li ser bêjeyê, carinan jî li ser hevokê çê dibe. [...] Guvaş bi piranî di bêjeyê de, di kîteya dawîn de ye. Mînak: Kemere, ‘kevir’ Darîye, ‘dara, das’ Hurak, ‘tevşo’ Pîya, ‘pevre’ Aspar, ‘siwar’ [...] 1.6. 1 Guvaş di Rewşa Bangkirinê de Li gorî guvaşê rewşa navdêran diguhere. Mînak: Hesen şî ware. ‘Hesen çû zozên.’ Li vir guvaş li ser kiteya dawî ye, nav jî nêr e û di rewşa xwerû de ye. Hesen, hela bê îta. ‘Hesen, hela were vir.’ Li vir guvaş li ser kiteya pêşî ye, nav jî nêr e û di rewşa bangkirinê de ye.
tone.locator: p. 126, §1.6 Guvaş (Stress) and §1.6.1 Guvaş di Rewşa Bangkirinê de
tone.translation: Stress arises in speech and is very important. Stress occurs on the syllable and on the word, and sometimes on the sentence. [...] Within the word, stress is mostly on the last syllable. Examples: Kemere 'stone', Darîye 'sickle', Hurak 'adze', Pîya 'together', Aspar 'rider'. [...] 1.6.1 Stress in the vocative: the state of nouns changes with the stress. Examples: Hesen şî ware 'Hesen went to the summer pasture' - here the stress is on the last syllable; the noun is masculine and in the plain (direct) state. Hesen, hela bê îta 'Hesen, come over here' - here the stress is on the first syllable; the noun is masculine and in the vocative.

tone.quote: Çekuyê makekê ke ebe /e/ u /i/ qedinê, gıraniya xo heceo verên ya ki wertên seroa. İyê ke ebe /a/ qedinê (neri u makek), ninu de qeydeo de nianên esto: Gıraniye heceo peyên seroa. Çekuyê ke neriê, gıraniya ni çekuyu ki tım heceo peyên seroa, ni çekuy ebe ni vokalu qedinê: /a/, /e/, /ê/, /i/, /o/, /ü/. [fn. 104: Tırki: vurgu, ağırlık]
tone.translation: Feminine words that end in /e/ and /i/ have their stress on the first or the middle syllable. For those that end in /a/ (masculine and feminine) the rule is this: the stress is on the last syllable. As for masculine words, their stress too is always on the last syllable; these words end in these vowels: /a/, /e/, /ê/, /i/, /o/, /ü/. [fn. 104: Turkish: vurgu 'stress', ağırlık 'weight']
